page: Amazon Web Services m8i.8xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro hypervisor-based virtual server featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The instance configuration provides 128.0 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 7 GHz, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 480 MB of L3 cache along with native support for advanced vector and matrix instruction extensions including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8.

Network infrastructure delivers a baseline bandwidth of 15 Gbps. The m8i.8xlarge instance does not include bundled local disk storage, discrete graphics processing units, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Persistent data requirements and root volumes must be provisioned through networked block storage services. This stateless storage profile isolates compute resources but introduces dependencies on remote disk throughput for input/output intensive applications.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core computational performance, with Geekbench results, cryptographic tests, and compressed file processing scoring in the upper quartile. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 34.31 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 226.42 GB/sec. The presence of AMX instructions facilitates solid CPU-based small-model machine learning inference and text processing. Conversely, uncached memory bandwidth and stress-ng throughput operate within the median 50% distribution, reflecting standard general-purpose tier efficiency rather than specialized memory-optimized throughput.

The Amazon Web Services m8i.8xlarge is matched for scalable enterprise web serving, backend application servers, container management nodes, software build environments, and CPU-bound vector acceleration tasks that do not mandate dedicated GPU hardware or local NVMe storage.
